title: How to Play Izzet Spellslingers
summary: Sequence cantrips, protect Veyran, and pick the right turn to convert spell volume into lethal pressure.

sections.heading: Opening Plan
sections.body: Keep hands with two or three lands, at least one cheap draw spell, and either a mana rock or an early payoff. The deck rewards patience, so spend the first turns sculpting a hand instead of exposing Veyran too early.

sections.heading: Midgame Priorities
sections.body: Develop one payoff at a time and leave mana open when possible. Storm-Kiln Artist and Archmage Emeritus are the best setup pieces because they turn every cantrip into mana or cards for the next spell.

sections.heading: Closing the Game
sections.body: Wait until you can chain several spells in one turn, preferably with Veyran doubling magecraft triggers. Past in Flames, Jeska's Will, and Thousand-Year Storm let the deck pivot from value to a decisive finish.

title: Piloting Golgari Graveyard Value
summary: Trade creatures early, build experience counters, and use the graveyard as a second hand until the table runs out of answers.

sections.heading: Opening Plan
sections.body: Prioritize ramp, a sacrifice outlet, and a creature that replaces itself. Sakura-Tribe Elder and Spore Frog are ideal because they are useful early and become repeatable tools once Meren is active.

sections.heading: Midgame Priorities
sections.body: Use removal creatures and edict effects to keep opposing boards manageable. Experience counters matter more than raw speed, so sequence sacrifices in a way that guarantees Meren has a strong target every end step.

sections.heading: Closing the Game
sections.body: Once Grave Pact effects or Blood Artist payoffs stick, every sacrifice becomes a problem for the table. Living Death and Gray Merchant of Asphodel provide the biggest swing turns after the graveyard is stocked.
